question: On canonical documents built from real parser output, does the Semantic Preservation Contract detect injected evidence faults, and is the repair scope it reports local to the damage rather than the whole document?
why_this_is_not_a_unit_test: tests/unit/test_semantic_preservation.py exercises the same invariants on hand-written fixtures whose blocks were authored to trip them.
Audit section 28-B asks for realistic parser outputs, fault injection, detection metrics and repair-locality metrics.

This runner builds every document from research/experiments/SEM-RISK-CONF-02/outputs/lane-a-native/, which are real extraction outputs over the frozen Lane A corpus (64 completed cases, GPU seconds 0.0, produced natively rather than by hand).
The faults are injected into those real documents, so a detection is a detection on production-shaped structure, not on a fixture built to fail.

inputs.case_selection: every case with status == completed and block_count >= 4, ordered by case_id; no sampling
inputs.provenance_note: These outputs are read only. This experiment writes nothing into SEM-RISK-CONF-02 and does not consume its inference budget.

construction.document_from_case: one CanonicalDocument per case; each parser text block becomes one CanonicalBlock with a SourceRef bound to that document version
construction.bindings_from_document: one SemanticEvidenceBinding per block, citing that block, with critical tokens drawn from the block's own text
construction.clean_expectation: a document with no injected fault must produce zero violations; any clean-case violation is a defect in the harness and aborts the run

fault_families.injection: a binding cites a block id that is not present in the document
one block's SourceRef is rewritten to a different document_version_id
a binding cites a table cell that belongs to no attached source block
a declared critical token is removed from the evidence text it was drawn from

negative_control.description: the unmodified document, run through the same path
negative_control.why: a detector that fires on clean documents has no discriminative value; this control is what separates detection from noise

metrics.detection_rate_per_family: detected / injected, reported separately for each fault family
metrics.false_positive_rate: clean documents reporting any violation / clean documents
metrics.repair_locality_blocks: quarantined blocks / total blocks in the document, per detected fault
metrics.repair_locality_pages: quarantined pages / total pages in the document, per detected fault
metrics.reported_as: counts first, ratios second; no confidence intervals are claimed at this cohort size

rationale.detection_rate_min_per_family: these are deterministic structural invariants, not statistical classifiers; a missed injection is a contract defect rather than a tolerable error rate
rationale.repair_locality_blocks_max_mean: a contract that quarantines more than half the document on a single-block fault provides no locality advantage over full reprocessing, which is the claim under test

limitations: Faults are injected synthetically. A real corruption may present differently, and the detection rate here is over injected faults, not over faults observed in the wild.
The corpus is Lane A born-digital pages; image-only pages are not represented.
Critical tokens are derived from the evidence text rather than declared by a domain expert, so token selection is mechanical.
